{{Short description|Mathematical term}}
In mathematics, an '''LLT polynomial''' is one of a family of [[symmetric function]]s introduced as [[q-analog|''q''-analogues]] of products of [[Schur polynomial|Schur functions]].<ref>[[Alain Lascoux]], Bernard Leclerc, and Jean-Yves Thibon [https://arxiv.org/abs/q-alg/9512031 Ribbon Tableaux, Hall-Littlewood Functions, Quantum Affine Algebras and Unipotent Varieties] {{MathSciNet|id=1434225}} J. Math. Phys. 38 (1997), no. 2, 1041–1068.</ref>

J. Haglund, [[M. Haiman]], and N. Loehr showed how to expand [[Macdonald polynomial]]s in terms of LLT polynomials.<ref>J. Haglund, M. Haiman, N. Loehr [https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0409538 A Combinatorial Formula for Macdonald Polynomials]{{MathSciNet|id=2138143}} J. Amer. Math. Soc. 18  (2005), no. 3, 735–761</ref> [[Ian Grojnowski]] and [[Mark Haiman]] proved a positivity conjecture for LLT polynomials that combined with the previous result implies the [[Macdonald polynomials#The Macdonald positivity conjecture|Macdonald positivity conjecture]] for [[Macdonald polynomials]], and extended the definition of LLT polynomials to arbitrary finite root systems.<ref>I. Grojnowski, M. Haiman, ''Affine algebras and positivity'' (preprint available [http://math.berkeley.edu/~mhaiman/ here])</ref>
